updated_reason: Added platform technical standards + QA rules as permanent guidelines
do: Include at least one specific numerical fact per video (years old, km/h, metres tall, cost in USD)
Name specific sub-locations, not just cities — e.g. 'Nanluogu Xiang alley' not just 'Beijing'
Open scene 0 with a QUESTION or unresolved tension — not a statement. Example: 'What if I told you this village has been here for 1,200 years — and almost nobody visits?'
Use second-person ('you') to make the viewer feel they are already there
Each narration must create curiosity for the NEXT scene — end lines slightly open, not conclusive
Every 3 scenes, introduce a contrast or unexpected twist (cheap vs expensive, ancient vs modern, crowded vs empty)
Visual queries must include: location + time of day + lighting condition + ONE emotional detail (e.g. 'mist rising', 'golden light', 'empty streets')
Visual queries must be cinematic and specific — imagine describing a shot to a film director, not a search engine
Keep each narration to 6-10 words — short-form Reels pace, not documentary narration
Target video length: ~32 seconds total (8 scenes × 4s) — every second must earn its place
avoid: Generic filler phrases: 'explore the unknown', 'vibrant city', 'breathtaking scenery', 'must-visit destination', 'incredible country', 'secrets of this country'
Sentences that could apply to any country — every line must be China-specific
Starting scenes with 'The' — sounds like a documentary, not a reel
Stacking adjectives without facts: 'stunning, beautiful, incredible' with no supporting detail
Ending sentences with 'always', 'every time', 'completely' — unnatural filler words
Repeating the same location across multiple scenes — each scene must be a different place
Visual queries that are just city names — 'China Shanghai skyline' tells a stock footage site nothing useful
CTA lines that say 'discover the secrets' — replace with something specific like 'More places like this. Follow us.'
style_notes: Narration tone: a well-travelled friend texting you tips, NOT a BBC documentary narrator
Think scroll-stopping: scene 0 must make someone pause their thumb in under 3 seconds
Contrast works best: ancient vs modern, cheap vs expected luxury, hidden vs famous
The CTA (last scene) should feel like a cliffhanger — hint at something you haven't shown yet

platform_standards._note: These are technical rules baked into the code. Listed here so the Director understands the constraints it is working within.
platform_standards.hook_card_rule: First 2 seconds = freeze frame with large hook text overlay (bold, box background). Must be readable at a glance.
platform_standards.subtitle_sizing: Font size = 3.2% of video height. ~34px for YouTube 1080p, ~61px for Instagram Reels 1920px.
platform_standards.subtitle_position: Bottom 18% of frame (y=82%). Clears Instagram UI chrome at bottom. Never goes lower.
platform_standards.subtitle_rule: Each cue shows for max 3.5s. No lingering. Text clears between thoughts.
platform_standards.video_formats: YouTube 1920x1080 (16:9) AND Reels 1080x1920 (9:16) — both generated from same source
platform_standards.tts_voice: Kokoro af_heart at 1.05x speed. Fallback to edge-tts AriaNeural.
platform_standards.qa_check: After every video: Claude Vision reviews 8-10 sampled frames for subtitle issues, hook readability, visual quality.

visual_query_rules: Always prefix with 'China' then the specific region/city
Include time of day: dawn, morning, midday, golden hour, dusk, night
Include weather/light mood: misty, golden light, overcast, clear blue sky, rainy
Include one human or natural movement detail: flowing water, walking monks, steam rising, lanterns swaying
Bad: 'China Beijing streets' — Good: 'China Beijing Hutong alley dawn golden light elderly man cycling'
example_good_narrations: What if I told you this 1,200-year-old town costs under ten dollars a night?
Three dollars gets you breakfast in this alley.
Locals eat standing up in streets unchanged since the Tang dynasty.
This is China's answer to the Amalfi Coast — almost nobody knows it.
example_bad_narrations: Experience breathtaking local culture every time.
Follow for more hidden China adventures and discover the secrets of this incredible country.
example_good_visual_queries: China Guilin Li River dawn mist cormorant fisherman bamboo raft golden light
China Chengdu Jinli Ancient Street night lanterns red glow wet cobblestones
China Zhangjiajie sandstone pillars sunrise sea of clouds aerial cinematic
China Xi'an Muslim Quarter morning food stall steam rising narrow alley warm light
